Thanks for the ping and the logs, Jordan — copying what I found after a quick look and some repro attempts in our staging mirror. TL;DR: looks like a request-path / payload edge-case causing an unhandled exception in the reranker service on the private deployment variant. Details and mitigation below.

What I saw:
- I replayed the exact request id you provided (req_7f8c9a) against our staging mirror — I can repro a 500 ~25% of the time when the reranker request includes a top-level "metadata" field with nested arrays (your client SDK appears to be sending an extra "context_chunks" array inside metadata). That additional nesting pushes the request parser into a codepath that tries to access a non-existent key, raising an exception.
- The 500s only appear on the private/VPC deployment path because we have a slightly older routing layer there (lockstep with some enterprise customers) that doesn't have the defensive checks we rolled out on hosted last month.

Immediate mitigations:
1) Short term: ask the Finlytics SDK to strip the extra metadata.context_chunks before calling the reranker. This will avoid the parser codepath and remove the 500s.
2) SDK suggestion: upgrade to redwood-js 1.0.0-beta (contains defensive parsing and a fix for this exact case).
3) Server-side patch: I’ll open a quick PR to add defensive checks to the private routing layer — target deploy tomorrow morning (2/26).

Requested repro artifacts from Finlytics (if you can provide these it will speed root cause):
- cURL that reproduces (with headers and body)
- Full request/response timeframe around req_7f8c9a (timestamps + request ids)
- Any proxy / gateway logs from your side (Envoy/http logs)

I’ll follow up once the patch is deployed and we’ve validated. Happy to jump on a short triage call if helpful.

- Marissa

--
